intro: The Bowthorpe Oak stands on Bowthorpe Park Farm at Manthorpe, near Bourne in Lincolnshire. Its hollow trunk is about thirteen metres round, which makes it one of the widest oaks in Britain, and the Tree Council named it among the 50 Great British Trees in 2002. A reader sent it to us with a photograph of the great barrel of a trunk, and the farm takes pre-booked tours.

trees.story:
A reader sent us this oak with a girth of 1,330 centimetres and an age of 1,000 to 1,300 years, and the photograph shows why. The trunk is a vast, hollow barrel of dark ridged bark, with the crown rising from it like a green dome and a fence set back to keep feet off the roots.

It stands at Bowthorpe Park Farm in Manthorpe, near Bourne in Lincolnshire. Wikipedia gives its circumference as about 13 metres, which makes it the second widest individual tree in Britain, behind the Marton Oak in Cheshire. The Tree Council chose it as one of the 50 Great British Trees in 2002, for the Queen's Golden Jubilee, and a BBC headline has called it a thousand years old. No ring count backs any age, so the honest range is the reader's, and a thousand years is the number most often repeated.

It is on private farmland. The farm takes pre-booked tours, and that is the way to see it up close; the reader's own photograph shows it from the edge of its fenced ring. If you have been, tell us on this page how you got in and what you saw.
trees.how_to_recognise: A very wide, hollow oak trunk inside a low fence on open farm grass, the crown spreading from the top of the barrel.
